note: (a)-(c) agree. On (d) the key is RIGHT and our original verdict was wrong. The statement is 'in an inelastic collision the final kinetic energy is ALWAYS less than the initial'. An inelastic collision is defined only by kinetic energy not being conserved, which also covers a collision that RELEASES stored internal energy (a latched compressed spring, an explosive collision), where the final kinetic energy exceeds the initial - so 'always' makes the statement false. Our original answer named that exception in a parenthesis and still recorded the verdict as True, i.e. the physics was present but the verdict a student reads was wrong.
